title: Blocked at $750
spec: M26 · the hook between the decision and the world
intro: The model decides to issue a $750 refund. Twenty lines of ordinary Python decide it does not happen. Watch where in the turn that decision lands.
foot: Run it for real: cd labs/M26-hooks-sessions-agent-sdk/solution && python support_agent.py

steps.title: The boring request first
narrative: Before the interesting failure, the shape of a normal turn. A customer asks for a filing lookup; the agent calls lookup_filing, then check_risk_profile, then stops. Two tool calls, two audit entries, nothing blocked.

The hooks were running the whole time. A PostToolUse hook with matcher "*" fires after every single tool execution, whether or not anything is wrong. That is the point: the audit trail is not something the model chooses to write, it is something the runtime writes on the model's behalf.
steps.youDo: Run python support_agent.py and read Scenario 1 before you read Scenario 2.

terminal.text: Look up filing UCC-2024-NY-0012847 and check for risk flags.

Turn 1: lookup_filing -> Active
    Turn 2: check_risk_profile -> LOW
    Turn 3: end_turn -> response delivered

steps.title: The model decides. The hook decides otherwise.
narrative: Request #2 is a refund for $750. The agent classifies it, composes the call, and fills in {"amount": 750.0} — the decision is made, the arguments are formed, the tool is about to run.

It does not run. A PreToolUse hook matched on issue_refund executes first, compares the amount against 500, and returns {"allowed": False, "reason": …}. No model is involved in that comparison. It is an if statement.
Watch where this sits. The block happens after the model has decided and before the world changes. Prompt rules live before the decision and can be talked around; a hook lives after it and cannot.
steps.claudeSays: The refund tool never executed. The agent receives {"blocked": true, "reason": …} where it expected a refund receipt, and has to do something with that.

terminal.text: I need a refund of $750 for duplicate filing charges.
Refund BLOCKED: Refund $750.00 exceeds $500 limit. Requires human approval.

state.label: issue_refund · the call that was composed

before.title: BEFORE — what the model handed to the runtime

after.title: AFTER — what the runtime handed back

data.reason: Refund $750.00 exceeds $500 limit. Requires human approval.

steps.title: Recovery is escalation, not retry
narrative: A blocked call is not the end of the turn. The agent reads the reason, treats it as a policy gap rather than a tool failure, and calls escalate_to_human with priority="high". That call is allowed, so it runs, and the PostToolUse hook logs it like everything else.

The customer gets a real answer with a real ticket number instead of a silent failure — and the audit trail now shows one BLOCKED sitting between three LOGGED entries. That row is the compliance artefact. It is what you show when someone asks whether the $500 limit held.

terminal.text: escalate_to_human(priority="high", reason="Refund of $750.00 exceeds automated limit")

I apologize, but I cannot process a refund of $750.00 automatically.
Refunds over $500 require human approval.
I have escalated your request (ticket: ESC-2024-0891).
Expected response time: 15 minutes.

Hook audit trail entries: 4
  Hooks blocked: 1

after.title: AFTER — the refund attempt is on the record

steps.title: Why not just write it in the prompt?
narrative: You could. In fact this lab does both: .claude/agents/refund-specialist.md tells the subagent "Never call issue_refund for amounts > $500 — the permission gate will deny it and waste a turn." That instruction is worth having, because it usually stops the wasted turn.

But the prompt is a suggestion the model is free to misread; the hook is a comparison Python performs. The lab puts the honest framing next to each other: prompts are probabilistic (~95%), hooks are deterministic (100%). Use prompts for tone and format, hooks for money, data access and compliance.

And keep the limits in view. A hook only sees calls that pass through the tool layer with a matching matcher — no matcher, no enforcement — and a blocked call still costs you a turn and tokens. It buys certainty, not efficiency.
steps.youDo: Change amount to 150.00 in Scenario 2 and re-run: the same hook, same code path, allows it and you get REF-2024-0042.
